# reselling_rootserver_firewall (Resource)

The own firewall rules of a rootserver, managed as a whole: rules that are not in the configuration are removed. Rules of firewall groups are not touched. Destroying the resource removes all own rules of the server. Import with the server id.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "reselling_rootserver_firewall" "web" {
  server_id = reselling_rootserver.web.id

  rules = [
    { direction = "in", action = "accept", protocol = "tcp", destination_port = "9100", source = "10.20.0.0/24", comment = "node exporter" },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `server_id` (String)

### Optional

- `rules` (Attributes List) Ordered rules; the first matching rule decides. Rules are matched to the existing ones by position. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The server id.

<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Required:

- `action` (String) `accept`, `drop` or `reject`.
- `direction` (String) `in` or `out`.

Optional:

- `comment` (String)
- `destination` (String) Destination address or network.
- `destination_port` (String) Port, range (`8000:8100`) or list (`80,443`).
- `enabled` (Boolean)
- `protocol` (String) `tcp`, `udp`, `icmp`, `icmpv6`, `gre`, `esp`, `ah`, `sctp`, `any` or `all`; any protocol when not set.
- `source` (String) Source address or network.
- `source_port` (String)

Read-Only:

- `id` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import id is the server id.
terraform import reselling_rootserver_firewall.web <server_id>
```
